title: Trump wants future Iran talks focused on nuclear file, not Hormuz, sources say
body: This detail matters less for immediate price action and more for how traders should read the ceiling on any near term de-escalation in the Strait of Hormuz. If Washington genuinely prefers to keep its own bilateral leverage reserved for Tehran's nuclear program rather than engaging directly on Hormuz access, that suggests the shipping and tolls track will continue to run through Oman and the Gulf states largely without direct US involvement, for better or worse. That could mean slower progress on a durable reopening framework, since the party with the most military leverage over the strait is choosing not to anchor its diplomacy there, but it could also mean less risk of the US complicating an Oman brokered deal with separate nuclear related demands. Either way, this points to continued reliance on regional diplomacy rather than a US-Iran breakthrough as the more likely path to easing the current oil risk premium, reinforcing why postponements like the one already covered are consequential rather than incidental. --- Earlier: Weekend: Tanker hit by projectile in Hormuz as fresh attacks reported at sea Oil gap higher: Saudi pipeline shut after drone attack as Hormuz meeting is postponed --- Washington appears content to let Iran, Oman and the Gulf states handle Hormuz diplomacy on their own, while keeping its own leverage with Tehran reserved for the nuclear question.

title: NZ services sector expands for third month as PSI rises to 51.2
body: The data adds to a modest but building case that New Zealand's services sector is stabilising, which matters for the Reserve Bank of New Zealand's read on domestic demand heading into upcoming policy decisions. A third consecutive month of expansion, with the three month moving average also climbing, gives some support to the view that the earlier contraction has passed, though the breadth of the improvement remains limited given three of the five sub-indices are still below the 50 threshold. Soft employment and activity sub-indices, alongside a majority of respondent comments turning negative on cost of living, interest rates, and election uncertainty, suggest this is not yet a signal for the NZD to lean heavily bullish on. Markets are likely to treat this as a modestly supportive but non-decisive data point rather than one that shifts the rate path narrative on its own. --- Eyes are not on the kwiwi $ right now: Oil gap higher: Saudi pipeline shut after drone attack as Hormuz meeting is postponed --- New Zealand's services sector notched its strongest reading since returning to growth, but with sentiment souring and half the sub-indices still in contraction, this looks like a fragile recovery rather than a solid turnaround. Summary: The BusinessNZ Performance of Services Index rose to 51.2 in August from 50.6 in July, marking a third consecutive month of expansion for the services sector.

title: Weekend: Tanker hit by projectile in Hormuz as fresh attacks reported at sea
body: Fresh attacks on shipping in the Strait of Hormuz land at a sensitive moment for oil, coming right as regional diplomacy over the waterway has stalled and just after the Saudi East-West pipeline closure removed an alternative export route. Confirmed damage to a single tanker would not typically move crude on its own, but the combination of a verified UKMTO incident and an unverified Iranian claim of a second, more serious attack reinforces the broader narrative of an unresolved and escalating threat to tanker traffic through one of the world's most important chokepoints. With shipping volumes through Hormuz already well below pre-war norms, incidents like this tend to reinforce existing risk premia rather than introduce a new one, keeping upside pressure on crude intact until the security picture stabilises or a credible ceasefire or shipping arrangement actually holds. --- Earlier: Iran says Hormuz meeting with Gulf states postponed at request of regional countries Globex is open and oil has jumped higher while stocks have slumped. Oil gap higher: Saudi pipeline shut after drone attack as Hormuz meeting is postponed --- Hormuz shipping came under attack again over the weekend, with a confirmed tanker fire and an unverified Iranian casualty claim adding fresh risk to an already fraught strait.

title: Oil gap higher: Saudi pipeline shut after drone attack as Hormuz meeting is postponed
body: This considerably raises the stakes for oil versus the weekend's initial framing of the Hormuz meeting postponement, since the pipeline closure removes a genuine safety valve rather than just delaying a diplomatic step. We gave the heads up to this attack a day or so before major news wires, had our ears to the ground we did: Vessels hit near Hormuz as satellite images fuel Saudi pipeline attack claims Brent oil surging. Houthi attack on Saudi East-West pipeline the likely culprit Unverified satellite data fuels talk of fresh hit on Saudi Arabia's East-West pipeline The East-West pipeline has been central to Saudi Arabia's ability to route crude away from Gulf chokepoints during the Iran war, with Aramco's own chief executive describing it as more important to market stability than the coordinated strategic reserve releases led by the United States. Its closure, combined with a fresh tanker attack in Hormuz producing a severe onboard fire and reports of Houthi forces advancing toward the Bab el-Mandeb Strait, points to supply risk building on multiple fronts simultaneously rather than easing. Expect this to reinforce the bid already seen in crude at the Globex open, with the risk skewed toward further upside pressure unless Riyadh moves quickly to clarify the extent of the pipeline damage and a realistic repair timeline.

title: Globex is open and oil has jumped higher while stocks have slumped.
body: The new week has opened with a classic risk off tone across Globex, crude gapping higher while equity index futures gapped lower at the open. The oil bid reflects the weekend's Strait of Hormuz development, with the postponed Iran and Gulf states meeting removing what had been seen as a step toward easing shipping disruption through the waterway, keeping the existing geopolitical premium intact rather than reducing it. On the equity side, weakness looks tied in part to Sam Altman's comments ruling out an OpenAI listing in 2026 on AI safety grounds, which has weighed on sentiment across AI linked tech names into the open. Together the two threads point to a session where energy is trading the conflict risk and equities are trading AI sector caution, rather than a single unifying catalyst, so follow through over the rest of the session will likely depend on which theme dominates headline flow from here. --- Earlier: Iran says Hormuz meeting with Gulf states postponed at request of regional countries Nasdaq futures set to open lower as Altman rules out 2026 OpenAI IPO --- The week has opened with oil bid on unresolved Middle East risk and stocks on the back foot after OpenAI's IPO retreat added to AI sector caution. Summary: Oil gapped higher and stock index futures gapped lower as the new week's Globex session opened.

title: Tesla's flying Roadster demo to land after years of missed reveal dates
body: The Roadster reveal is unlikely to move Tesla's share price in any lasting way on its own, given the stock is currently priced by the market largely on robotics and software narratives rather than a low volume halo car. Where it could matter is sentiment and credibility. Tesla shares closed recently around $365, against an average analyst target near $377, a gap of roughly 3%, leaving relatively little room for the market to reward another spectacle style demo without a firmer production timeline attached. Musk has missed several previous Roadster reveal dates going back to the original 2017 unveiling, so some coverage is framing October 1 as a test of whether Tesla can convert hype into an actual delivery date rather than a repeat teaser. A clean demonstration with a credible build schedule could support sentiment modestly, while another delay or a demo seen as gimmicky risks reinforcing skepticism already priced into the stock's tight gap to target. --- Earlier: Nasdaq futures set to open lower as Altman rules out 2026 OpenAI IPO --- Tesla is finally set to show its Roadster on October 1, but with the flashy SpaceX thrusters reserved for a non-road-legal special edition, the real question for investors is whether a build date finally follows the spectacle. Summary: Tesla will reveal its second generation Roadster on October 1 in Waco, Texas, after multiple missed reveal dates dating back to the car's original 2017 unveiling.

title: Brent Jumps on Saudi Pipeline Shutdown
body: Brent crude climbed toward $108 a barrel—its highest level in four months—after gaining more than 9% last week, as Saudi Arabia shut a major crude pipeline following drone attacks, disrupting a key route that bypasses the Strait of Hormuz. Saudi Arabia suspended operations on the East–West pipeline as a precaution after Thursday's attacks and has not yet indicated when flows will resume. At the same time, talks between Iran and several Gulf states on creating a temporary shipping corridor through the Strait of Hormuz were postponed, according to Oman's Foreign Minister, Badr Albusaidi. Reports indicated that Saudi Arabia had reservations about the plan, while Bahrain said it would not take part. The closure of the East–West pipeline has underscored its critical role in sustaining energy supplies across the Middle East, especially as the United States and Iran remain deadlocked over control and security of Hormuz. The pipeline, which runs across Saudi Arabia to ports on the Red Sea, has a capacity of about 7 million barrels per day. The material has been provided by InstaForex Company - www.instaforex.com

title: NZX 50 Trades in the Green to Start the Week
body: The NZX 50 rose 95 points, or 0.7%, to 13,676 in Monday morning trade, recouping the prior session's losses and rebounding from Friday's trough, its lowest level since June 29. The advance was led primarily by materials, healthcare, and financial stocks. Sentiment was supported by fresh data showing that New Zealand's private-sector expansion remains solid, with services activity recording its strongest increase in eight months. Tourist arrivals also climbed to a four-month high, further underpinning confidence. Gains were limited, however, as investors stayed cautious ahead of this week's release of New Zealand's Q2 GDP figures and a series of key economic indicators from China, the country's largest trading partner. A decline in US stock futures, set against rising oil prices and mounting concerns around AI safety, also tempered risk appetite. Among the early movers, EBOS Group advanced 2.3%, Fisher & Paykel added 1.6%, Freightways Group gained 0.8%, Infratil increased 1.2%, and F&C Investment rose 0.6%.
